summary: Checkpoint 2.5k (lowest error so far). Over all 32 held-out clips the median hand error is 25 px for the trained model vs 112 px for the base model; it beats the base on 31 of 32 clips.

items.prompt: the potato masher ends up lifted in the left hand.
items.note: Trained model 8.9 px vs base 85.6 px: essentially as close as the real clip (8.5 px).

items.prompt: the red spatula ends up turned in the right hand.
items.note: 8.9 px vs base 65.9 px; the hand turns the spatula along the target path.

items.prompt: the white mug ends up turned in the right hand.
the red spatula ends up moved to the left and farther and turned.
the ranch bottle ends up lifted in both hands and turned.
the patterned mug ends up in the left hand and turned.
the tomato sauce can ends up lifted in the left hand and turned.
items.note: A real miss: both hands drift from their targets (45 and 64 px) and are not detected in about a quarter of the frames.

items.prompt: the parmesan can ends up set down to the right and farther and turned, and the orange juice carton ends up lifted in the right hand and turned.
items.note: The right hand follows its target closely (17.5 px). The left hand is in view for a single frame, is missed, and is capped at 128 px. The per-clip average weights it equally with the right hand.

items.prompt: the hands move without touching anything.
items.note: Eval artifact more than a failure: the generated hand sits on the target skeleton, but the hand detector labels it a RIGHT hand while the target is the LEFT hand, so the metric counts the left hand as missing (capped at 128 px).
